title.title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for matrix products
title.subtitle: Claim: iterated matrix multiplication needs $n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$ gates in homogeneous depth-five circuits

plain: Multiply many grids of variables: shallow five-layer formulas for it need about $n^{\sqrt n}$ steps, and that is enough

beats.text: The polynomial: the top-left entry of a product of $n$ matrices of variables
Sums of products, five layers deep, every gate homogeneous
Claimed: lower and upper bounds meet at $n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$, over characteristic zero

steps: Score each polynomial by the rank of a matrix
Small five-layer circuits only reach a low score
Matrix products score high, so circuits must be huge
A matching construction shows that size is enough

after.label: Claimed, 25 Sep 2026
after.note: homogeneous depth five, any bottom linear forms

achievement.note: Syntactic homogeneity is essential; general depth five is not covered

voice.text: The top corner of a product of n matrices, five layers deep.
A rank score is low for small circuits and high for matrix products.
Claimed: n to the root n, both ways.

sources.quote: has at least n^{sqrt(n)/400} gates for large n, with arbitrary bottom linear forms; a matching n^{sqrt(n)+4} upper bound holds over every field
Homogeneous depth-4 lower bounds n^{Omega(sqrt n)} for IMM (Kayal-Limaye-Saha-Srinivasan; Kumar-Saraf, ~2014)
Homogeneity is syntactic and essential; general (non-homogeneous) depth-5 is not covered.
